source_batch.unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 3: FEMA — Classify current and capital account transactions without confusing classification with permission

facts.statement: Courseware distinguishes capital changes in the specified cross-border assets/liabilities from current-account payments and gives trade, services, interest, family maintenance, education and medical expenses as current examples.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 170; PDF page = printed page + 19

facts.statement: Capital-account definition includes contingent liabilities and the specified resident/non-resident asset-liability changes; current account excludes capital account and includes the named ordinary-business payments. Section 5 permits current-account forex through an authorised person subject to prescribed restrictions. Section 6 separates RBI debt-instrument specification from Central Government non-debt prescription, with consultation and conditions.

payload.title: Classify the economic effect, then check permission
payload.core_explanation_md:
For a **capital account transaction**, inspect whether the transaction changes the specified cross-border assets or liabilities, including contingent liabilities. For a **current account transaction**, the Act gives examples such as ordinary foreign-trade/service payments, loan interest, family maintenance and education or medical expenses.

Classification is only the first step. “Current” does not mean that the bank may ignore applicable restrictions, and “capital” does not mean that every such transaction is absolutely prohibited. The bank must identify the permitted route, conditions and documentary requirements after classifying the transaction. Keep the classification note and the permission check separate in the file.

self_check.prompt_text: Why does calling a transaction current account not finish the compliance decision?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Applicable restrictions, authorised-person requirements and documentation still need to be satisfied.

payload.title: Contingent obligations matter; authority also depends on the instrument
payload.core_explanation_md:
The capital-account definition expressly includes **contingent liabilities**. A reviewer must therefore look beyond an immediate cash movement or a balance-sheet cash entry. A new cross-border obligation can require analysis even before any payment occurs.

The statutory copy also distinguishes the regulatory roles for capital transactions involving debt instruments and those not involving debt instruments: Section 6 assigns specification/prescription roles to RBI and the Central Government respectively, with consultation. The current instrument classification and operative rules still need verification; do not assume one authority or one old rule governs every capital request.

self_check.prompt_text: Can absence of an immediate cash payment by itself rule out capital-account analysis?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The definition includes contingent liabilities, so the obligation and statutory conditions must be examined.

payload.stem_md: A branch labels an ordinary overseas service-invoice payment current account, then omits the applicable restrictions check. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text_md: Every service payment is a capital transaction because money leaves India
options.explanation_md: Cross-border movement alone does not turn an ordinary service payment into a capital transaction.

options.text_md: Current-account classification removes the authorised-person requirement
options.explanation_md: The statutory route and any applicable restrictions remain relevant.

options.text_md: The classification can be appropriate, but it does not establish that every permission condition is met
options.explanation_md: The economic classification and the transaction-specific compliance decision are separate steps.

options.text_md: An invoice supplied by the customer overrides all FEMA rules
options.explanation_md: A commercial document supports purpose evidence; it cannot override the governing legal requirements.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The economic classification and the transaction-specific compliance decision are separate steps.

payload.stem_md: A proposed cross-border arrangement creates a contingent liability but no immediate payment. Why should the reviewer avoid ruling out capital-account implications solely on cash movement?

options.text_md: The capital-account definition expressly includes contingent liabilities
options.explanation_md: The liability effect can matter before cash is paid; no immediate payment is not a sufficient exclusion test.

options.text_md: Every transaction without cash is outside FEMA
options.explanation_md: FEMA definitions and transaction rules are not confined to immediate cash transfers.

options.text_md: All contingent liabilities are automatically permitted with no conditions
options.explanation_md: Inclusion in the definition does not establish permission or remove conditions.

options.text_md: A contingent liability can exist only in Indian rupees
options.explanation_md: The currency assertion is unsupported and does not address the statutory inclusion of contingent liabilities.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The liability effect can matter before cash is paid; no immediate payment is not a sufficient exclusion test.

payload.stem_md: An internal manual says all capital-account instrument rules are made by the same authority under an identical statutory power. Which distinction in the retrieved Section 6 text should the reviewer check?

options.text_md: Whether the remittance exceeds a particular bank internal transaction limit
options.explanation_md: An internal amount limit does not allocate the statutory debt/non-debt instrument-making roles.

options.text_md: RBI alone exercises an identical delegated power for every debt and non-debt capital transaction
options.explanation_md: The retrieved Section 6 text assigns distinct debt and non-debt roles with consultation; it does not use one identical power for every instrument.

options.text_md: All non-debt transactions fall outside FEMA
options.explanation_md: The text expressly includes a Central Government role for non-debt capital transactions.

options.text_md: The debt-instrument and non-debt-instrument provisions allocate distinct roles
options.explanation_md: The copy distinguishes RBI specification and Central Government prescription, with consultation and conditions.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The copy distinguishes RBI specification and Central Government prescription, with consultation and conditions.
